newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian vehicle sales to Sept up 0.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian vehicle sales to Sept up 0.4 pct.

text.p: Australian vehicle sales for 1996 to September were up 0.4 percent from the same period a year earlier, the Federal Chamber of Automotive Industries (FCAI) said on Monday.
Vehicle sales for nine months to September totalled 484,661, up from 482,547 a year earlier, the industry organisation said in its monthly VFACTS publication.
Sales in September totalled 51,032, up from 49,990 a year earlier. In August, total sales were 54,778.
The FCAI has forecast total Australian vehicle sales of 640,000 for 1996, up 10,000 from 1995.
Heavy truck sales amounted to 11,150 for the year to September, down from 13,438 a year earlier after sales of 1,231 in September, up from 1,137 a year earlier.
"The market remains flat despite the introduction of a myriad of new models," the FCAI said.
"The daily selling rate year-to-date September 1996 stands at 2,132.3 versus 2,123.0 for the same period in 1995, an increase of a mere 9.3 vehicles per day," the chamber said.
Passenger car sales to September totalled 367,326, up from 365,679 a year earlier after sales of 38,617 in September, up from 38,599 in September 1995.
Truck sales for the year to date total 117,335 compared with 116,868 a year earlier after September sales of 12,415, up from 11,391 a year earlier.
Within the total truck sales light truck sales totalled 106,185 for the year to September, up from 103,430 a year earlier after sales of 11,184 in September, up from 10,254 in September 1995.

Among the vehicle manufacturers with plants in Australia, Ford Motor Co maintained its market lead in the year to date with sales of 97,581 vehicles for a market share of 20.1 percent but this was down from a year earlier when sales of 102,524 vehicles represented market share of 21.2 percent.
General Motors Co increased its market share to 19.8 percent with sales of 96,098 vehicles, up from 93,314 a year earlier when its market share was 19.3 percent.
Toyota Motor Co sold 88,636 vehicles for an 18.3 percent share of the market. In the year to September 1995 Toyota sold 89,725 vehicles, which represented a market share of 18.6 percent.

Mitsubishi Motors Corp, the fourth car manufacturer in Australia, sold 44,712 vehicles in the year to September for a market share of 9.2 percent, down from 10.3 percent a year earlier when sales totalled 49,913.
The remainder of the sales total was made up by imports, led by Hyundai Motor Co with sales of 38,336 vehicles making up 7.9 percent of the total.
A year earlier, the South Korean car maker sold 25,897 vehicles for a market share of 5.4 percent.
